title: Steam Deck OLED Review Roundup: Still the One to Beat?
description: Volt’s research-based verdict on the Steam Deck OLED: the gorgeous screen and better battery reviewers love, and why it isn’t a performance upgrade.
intro: Valve’s refreshed handheld swapped in a stunning HDR OLED screen and a bigger battery. Reviewers call it the definitive Steam Deck, but not a Steam Deck 2.
verdict: The best-value PC handheld, now with a gorgeous screen. Same performance, though.
pros: Vivid HDR OLED screen with deep blacks and a 90Hz refresh rate
Better battery life and faster charging than the original
Faster Wi-Fi and the easy SteamOS experience
cons: No real performance boost; demanding new games can struggle
Battery is still a weak spot in heavy games
bestFor: PC gamers with a Steam library who want a polished handheld.
skipIf: You already own an original Steam Deck and mostly play docked.
cardText: The best-value PC handheld, with a gorgeous screen but the same power.

sections.h2: Why everyone is talking about it
sections.html: The Steam Deck is still the handheld every new PC handheld is compared to, and the OLED model is the version most reviewers recommend.

Tom’s Guide called it the best the device has ever been. TechRadar called it the definitive Steam Deck but harder to justify for existing owners. Stuff summed it up as the ultimate first-generation Steam Deck rather than a sequel. Everyone praised the screen; battery gains were welcome but not dramatic, and performance is unchanged.
For a new buyer with Steam games, it’s still the smart choice. Compare it with the pricier ROG Xbox Ally X and the Switch 2 in our handheld comparison.
